Snow closes the pass for at least five months of the year, and people cross it only sporadically in the months when it is passable. It is a basic road – an unpaved track covered with gravel. On the other side of the border, there is no Chinese customs facility, and China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has not commented on the road’s opening. For the moment, the road leads to a closed border, with no indication of when Beijing might open it to commercial traffic. The Wakhan Corridor is a narrow protruding stretch of land extending for about 350 kilometres (220 miles). It lies between Tajikistan to the north and Pakistan to the south, but is entirely within Afghan territory, connecting it with China. TEHRAN – The Persian translation of the book “Small Country,” the debut novel by the Franco-Rwandan rapper, songwriter, and novelist, Gaël Faye, has been released in the Iranian book market. Translated by Maryam Saberi, the book has been published by Cheshmeh Publication in 175 pages, ISNA reported. Originally published in 2016, the book has since been translated into 36 languages. “Small Country” opens with the 33-year-old narrator, Gabriel, reflecting on his life in France. Unable to let go of his past, Gabriel makes the decision to return to Burundi, the country of his childhood and the birthplace of the author, as the novel's main story begins. Set in Burundi and Rwanda from 1993 onwards, the novel is subsequently narrated by ten-year-old Gaby, who lives with his French father and Rwandan mother in an impasse in a comfortable district of Bujumbura, Burundi. Gabriel's sheltered upbringing leaves him oblivious to the increasing tensions between the Hutu majority and the Tutsi minority (to which he, through his mother, belongs). As neighboring Rwanda faces the outbreak of civil war and genocide, which spill over into Burundi, the innocence of Gaby and his group of friends is brutally shattered. The novel is based on Faye's own experiences growing up in Burundi during this period; the author has, however, stressed that it is not strictly autobiographical. Faye used his advantage of adult perspective to write about a boy who went through a similar situation to him as a child.

full_text: 'That’s what they deserve' — Zakharova about TASS’ expulsion from EANA Earlier on Friday, the EANA General Assembly expelled TASS, whose membership was suspended back in March 2022 MOSCOW, November 13. /TASS/. Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova has commented on TASS's expulsion from the European Alliance of News Agencies (EANA) by saying that Europe "deserves" it. Earlier on Friday, the EANA General Assembly expelled TASS, whose membership was suspended back in March 2022. At the same time, the alliance voted to admit Lithuania’s news agency ELTA. After expelling TASS and admitting Lithuania’s ELTA, EANA continues to have 33 members.

full_text: Churchill’s WWII bunker opens to visitors — newspaper The Fan Bay Deep Shelter was home to some of the most advanced military technology of its time, The Telegraph reported LONDON, November 13. /TASS/. A World War II bunker built on the orders of then-British Prime Minister Winston Churchill has opened to visitors for the first time, The Telegraph reported. The Fan Bay Plotting Room was constructed four meters underground beneath the White Cliffs of Dover in southeastern England in 1940. According to the newspaper, it was "home to some of the most advanced military technology of its time, helping to direct the artillery defending the Strait of Dover from German shelling." The site was abandoned in the 1970s, with its entrance buried under soil. It was rediscovered in 2017 and became the focus of National Trust research and conservation.

The IRS issued $84 billion in tax refunds this March, about $25 billion less than they issued in March of 2022, according to BofA analysts. That led consumers to pull back in spending at department stores and on durable goods, such as appliances and furniture. Spending at general merchandise stores fell 3% in March from the prior month and spending at gas stations declined 5.5% during the same period. Excluding gas station sales, retail spending retreated 0.6% in March from February. However, retail spending rose 2.9% year-over-year. A Vietnam Airlines Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner operating a Munich-Hanoi flight returned to Munich Airport on Saturday after reportedly suffering a serious incident during takeoff, according to flight-tracking website Flightradar24 and the airline. Flight VN-34, operated by Boeing 787-9 aircraft VN-A867, reportedly rotated extremely late during takeoff and overran the runway before becoming airborne. Preliminary reports said the aircraft travelled around 120 metres beyond the runway end, entering the grass and coming close to the first row of approach lights. The aircraft also reportedly suffered a tailstrike and tyre damage. After takeoff, the aircraft climbed to around 10,000 feet before the crew received a tyre-pressure indication and decided to dump fuel before returning to Munich. Flightradar24 said the aircraft circled for more than two hours to burn fuel. Around 90 minutes after departure, the Boeing 787 made two low approaches to Munich's Runway 26R before landing safely. Smoke was reportedly seen coming from the left main landing gear, after which the aircraft became disabled on the runway. Passengers were evacuated using emergency slides, with the fire brigade present at the scene, according to Flightradar24. Vietnam Airlines said the Hanoi-bound flight returned to its departure airport due to a "technical issue", without providing further details.
